items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the arts and cultural affairs law, in relation to ticket
websites; the online resale of tickets to places of entertainment; the sale of
tickets to places of entertainment; the licensing fee for ticket resellers;
ticket resellers operating a retail ticket purchasing platform provide a link
to a copy of their license; and the resale of tickets to places of
entertainment; to amend chapter 704 of the laws of 1991, amending the arts and
cultural affairs law and chapter 912 of the laws of 1920 relating to the
regulation of boxing and wrestling matches relating to tickets to places of
entertainment, in relation to the effectiveness thereof; and to amend chapter
151 of the laws of 2010, amending the arts and cultural affairs law relating
to resale of tickets to places of entertainment, in relation to the
effectiveness thereof
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8501

SPONSOR: MURPHY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the arts and cultural affairs law, in relation to ticket
websites; the online resale of tickets to places of entertainment; the
sale of tickets to places of entertainment; the licensing fee for ticket
resellers; ticket resellers operating a retail ticket purchasing plat-
form provide a link to a copy of their license; and the resale of tick-
ets to places of entertainment; to amend chapter 704 of the laws of
1991, amending the arts and cultural affairs law and chapter 912 of the
laws of 1920 relating to the regulation of boxing and wrestling matches
relating to tickets to places of entertainment, in relation to the
effectiveness thereof; and to amend chapter 151 of the laws of 2010,
amending the arts and cultural affairs law relating to resale of tickets
to places of entertainment, in relation to the effectiveness thereof

 
PURPOSE:

To extend the current article 25 of the arts and cultural affairs law,
which is set to expire on June 30, 2018, and to enact a number of
reforms that will provide fairness measures and additional transparency
for consumers accessing and purchasing tickets to places of enter-
tainment.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends arts and cultural affairs law to add a new section
25.34 that will prohibit the practice of "URL fraud", using websites
that closely resemble official websites for ticket purchases to direct
consumers to the website of an entity not affiliated with the venue or
performers selling such tickets, and contains a penalty structure for
violations of this prohibition.

Section 2 amends arts and cultural affairs law section 25.23 to require
ticket sale operators or their agents to inform consumers when a ticket
is being sold by licensed ticket reseller in the secondary ticket
market. It also requires online ticket marketplaces to inform consumers
that tickets listed there are on the secondary market, that a ticket's
price may exceed the established price of such ticket, and provide the
marketplace's refund policy.

Section 3 amends arts and cultural affairs law section 25.07 to require
primary sellers of tickets to establish a refund policy in the same
manner that secondary ticket resellers currently do.

Section 4 amends arts and cultural affairs law section 25.13 to reduce
the annual licensure fee for ticket resellers from $5,000 to $2,500.

Section 5 amends arts and cultural affairs law section 25.19 to ensure
that ticket reseller licensees selling on ticket sale platforms post
hyperlinks to copies of their licenses in the same manner as they
current do for online sales.

Section 6 amends the arts and cultural affairs law to add a new section
25.10 that will prohibit the practice of "speculative ticketing",
reselling a ticket when the reseller does not have possession of the
ticket or is in a written contract to obtain the ticket.
Section 7 amends arts and cultural affairs law section 25.07 to require
operators of a place of entertainment and ticket resellers to disclose
the total price of a ticket, and the portion of the price that repres-
ents a service charge, fee, or surcharge, prior to accepting payment for
the ticket.

Sections 8 and 9 extend the current provisions of the arts and cultural
affairs law article 25 that are set to expire on June 30, 2018 to June
30, 2023.

Section 10: Establishes the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Currently, arts and cultural affairs law article 25 governs the sale of
tickets to places of entertainment. In the 2010 legislative session,
significant changes were made to the regulation of the sale and resale
of tickets to places of entertainment. As the ticket market evolves,
ensuring the protection of consumers and their rights becomes increas-
ingly important.

This bill seeks to provide additional fairness measures by combating URL
fraud and speculative ticketing practices. It also provides enhanced
disclosure provisions, including notification of a ticket's sale on the
secondary market, primary seller refund policies, reseller license
disclosure on ticket purchasing platforms, and the total price of tick-
ets before completion of a transaction, that will afford consumers a
more equitable market for purchasing tickets to and ultimately enjoying
performances.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately; provided, however, that section
25.34 of the arts and cultural affairs law, as added by section one of
this act, shall survive the expiration and reversion of article 25 of
such law as provided in section 4 of chapter 704 of the laws of 1991, as
amended; and provided, further, that the amendments to article 25 of the
arts and cultural affairs law made by sections two, three, four, five,
six and seven of this act, shall not affect the repeal and reversion of
such article and shall be deemed repealed therewith.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8501A

SPONSOR: MURPHY
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the arts and cultural affairs law, in
relation to the sale of tickets to places of entertainment; to amend
chapter 704 of the laws of 1991, amending the arts and cultural affairs
law and chapter 912 of the laws of 1920 relating to the regulation of
boxing and wrestling matches relating to tickets to places of enter-
tainment; and chapter 151 of the laws of 2010, amending the arts and
cultural affairs law relating to resale of tickets to places of enter-
tainment, in relation to extending the effectiveness of the provisions
thereof

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This bill would reform the New York ticket resale law in order to
increase transparency and fairness for consumers of New York.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 adds a new § 25.10 of the Arts and Cultural Affairs Law to
place certain requirements on ticket resellers who sell tickets they do
not own at the time of sale.

Section 2 amends § 25.19 of the Arts and Cultural Affairs Law to require
ticket resellers to provide their license number on any online ticket
purchasing platform on which they sell tickets, or provide a hyperlink
that allows for such posting.

Section 3 amends § 25.23 of the Arts and Cultural Affairs Law to require
online ticket resale marketplaces to post a clear and conspicuous notice
on their website stating that their website is being used for the
secondary sale of tickets.

Section 4 amends § 25.24 of the Arts and Cultural Affairs Law to add a
new subdivision 10 that would provide that any ticket reseller who know-
ingly uses ticket purchasing software, or owns or controls ticket
purchasing software, may lose their license and be barred from licensure
as a ticket reseller for up to three years for such use or ownership of
such software.

Section 5 amends § 25.07 of the Arts and Cultural Affairs Law to require
operators or their agents and ticket resellers to disclose in a clear
and conspicuous manner all fees and surcharges associated with the
purchase of tickets.

Section 6 adds a new § 25.12 of the Arts and Cultural Affairs Law to
allow professional sports organizations to offer nontransferable member-
ship passes to a specific number of events in a specified period of time
at discounted prices.

Section 7 amends § 25.30 of the Arts and Cultural Affairs Law by adding
a new subdivision 5 that requires operators to provide a clear and
conspicuous disclosure to purchasers if such purchasers are transferred
to a ticket seller in the secondary market.

Section 8 adds a new § 25.34 to the Arts and Cultural Affairs Law to
prohibit the use of a name in a website or a URL that is intended to
confuse the public into thinking they are buying a ticket directly from
an operator or operator's agent when in fact they are on a secondary
market website with a confusingly similar name to the name of the opera-
tor or its agent.

Section 9 and 10 extend the effective date for the laws relating to
tickets to places of entertainment to June 20, 2021.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Everyday New Yorkers are denied fair access to tickets by resellers who
distort the market, obscure information that allows for better purchas-
ing decisions, and gouge fans with excessive prices and fees. In 2016,
The Office of New York State Attorney General released a report exposing
the unscrupulous practices of the industry and making it clear that
reforms are critical to protect consumers.  This bill will reform this
system to create a fairer and more transparent market place that allows
New Yorkers a fair shot at fairly priced tickets.

Specifically, this bill would address the practice of selling "specula-
tive tickets" - i.e. tickets that a reseller does not have and does not
have a right to sell. The practice is widespread, even though specula-
tive ticket listings are often deceptive and illegal under New York's
existing consumer protection laws. This bill would clarify existing law,
and expressly require a clear, conspicuous disclosure in plain language
when a reseller is making an offer to obtain a ticket.  This bill would
also add new consumer protections requiring that consumers expressly
confirm that they understand what they are purchasing before a trans-
action can occur, and that resellers provide refunds to consumers who
have not yet received a ticket or received a different ticket that was
advertised. In addition, this bill would clarify that resellers cannot
evade New York's existing consumer protection laws by complying with
these provisions if their speculative ticket listings are otherwise
deceptive and illegal.

Lastly, this bill allows professional sports organizations to offer
nontransferable membership passes which are comprised of discounted
tickets to a specific number of games in a specified time period.  These
membership passes are now offered in many other states and have been
successful in allowing professional sporting events to be more afforda-
ble for and accessible to the general public.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None to the State.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Section 11 provides that this act shall take effect immediately;
provided however that: (a) sections one, two, three, four, five, seven
and eight of this act shall take effect on the one hundred eightieth day
after it shall have become a law; and (b) the amendments to article 25
of the arts and cultural affairs law made by sections one, two, three,
five, seven and eight of this act shall not affect the repeal of such
article and shall be deemed repealed therewith.
